text:
rico: Observed inconsistent termination for stream generators in python SDK. When server sends only a final newline then closes, async generator sometimes never yields final event and aclose() blocks.

anya: Can you paste a tiny repro? sync or async?

rico: Async:
```py
agen = client.stream_text(model="mini")
async for chunk in agen:
    if chunk.get("done"):
        break
```

rico: Env: py3.11, redwood-py 0.9.3, aiohttp transport, nginx ingress.

sam: Likely SSE parsing: EOF (zero-length read) isn't treated like an empty-line delimiter, so parser awaits more data.

anya: Did you try agen.aclose()?

rico: Yep; hangs in low-level read. Cancelling task leaves sockets in loop.

sam: Short fixes: treat EOF as event terminator and add a small read-timeout fallback. Long term: expose Stream object with explicit close()/cancel() for sync+async.

devx-bot: Ticket RDW-STREAMS-5 created to track public Stream API proposal.

ops: CI flaky: test_stream_cancel on linux-aio failing intermittently. Filed INF-4123.

anya: Workaround for users: wrap iteration in asyncio.wait_for per-iteration and call agen.aclose() in finally. Not ideal but workable.

sam: I'll open PR to synthesize final event on EOF and add unit tests for (1) final "
" then FIN and (2) immediate EOF with no newline. Will also mirror fixes to sync path and update type hints to Iterator[Mapping] so quickstarts don't confuse users.

rico: Thanks 7 please ping here when PR lands and I'll validate against our ingress.

anya: Keeping thread for follow-ups.
